question: In tetrahedron $ABCD$ , edge $AB$ has length 3 cm. The area of face $ABC$ is $15\mbox{cm}^2$ and the area of face $ABD$ is $12 \mbox { cm}^2$ . These two faces meet each other at a $30^\circ$ angle. Find the volume of the tetrahedron in $\mbox{cm}^3$ .

These two faces meet at a 30-degree angle. Hmm, right. Let me recall how the volume of a tetrahedron is calculated. The formula is (1/3) times the base area times the height, right? That angle is called the dihedral angle between the two faces. Dihedral angle is the angle between two planes, in this case, the planes of triangles ABC and ABD.

V = (2 * A1 * A2 * sin θ) / (3 * |AB|)
